issue.title: sase-core tool_run store contention tests hit SQLite busy timeouts under the loaded check lane

task_type_fields.evidence:
Proposed by footprint phase sase-1p1.12--4 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #5) on 2026-10-28. While it verified the sase-core footprint export/import commit, `sase tool run check` in sase-core (ToolRun witness e806578cc8f9fec509172149f2c41b66) failed two Rust tests under the full parallel check with SQLite busy/WAL lock timeouts:

- tool_run::store::tests::contention::barrier_orders_exclusive_holder_then_show
- tool_run::store::tests::contention::retry_after_releasable_lock_does_not_duplicate_run

Both passed when rerun in isolation on the unchanged tree, and the phase's footprint code does not touch tool_run. Fail rate: 1 of 1 loaded full checks, 0 isolated failures. The lock holder was not identified. The symptom matches the sase-side ToolRun store-busy family (sase-18t), but these are separate Rust nodes in sase-core with their own timeouts, so the root cause may differ.
task_type_fields.repro_cmd: sase tool run check (in sase-core, loaded host)

issue.creation_reason: A footprint phase saw two sase-core ToolRun contention tests fail under a loaded check and pass in isolation; no existing task tracks these Rust nodes.

payload.description: Same symptom family (ToolRun SQLite store busy under load) on the sase side; check for a shared lock-holder root cause

payload.entry:
Fixed in the sase-1ou landing. The flake was caused by that epic: core commit 6d11122e (sase-1ou.2.1.1) added tool_run/store/tests/contention.rs.
- Cause: the releasable-lock tests asserted success within the 250 ms production default while a separately scheduled thread dropped an exclusive lock, which also runs a close-time checkpoint. Under load that release outlasts 250 ms.
- Test fix: release schedules use an explicit 10 s RELEASE_BUDGET and release only after the contender thread starts. New zero_budget_waits_the_core_default_before_busy pins the production default deterministically: with an unreleased holder the call ends Busy, elapsed is at least the default and below the cap. wal_reserved_writer_coexists_with_readonly_show drops a redundant wall-clock bound; success while RESERVED is held is the oracle.
- The same stress exposed an epic regression in the store. A call whose budget was already spent before its first open, or whose corrupt-store quarantine outlasted the budget, returned Busy with no contender. The pre-6d11122e code always reopened after a quarantine.
- Store fix in connection.rs: every call is owed one open, a quarantine is owed one recreate, and the WAL conversion attempts once before honoring its deadline. New spent_budget_still_owes_the_first_open and slow_quarantine_still_recreates_the_store fail on the old code and pass on the fix.
- Stress (same loop before and after: 200 runs of the tool_run::store tests at --test-threads=64, 24 parallel processes, 96 CPU spinners plus 4 dsync writers): before, 75 of 200 runs failed (barrier_orders 42, releasable 34, retry 27, wal_reserved 9, concurrent_begins 1, corrupt_store 4). After, 0 of 200.
- All 258 tool_run tests pass. sase-core guarded check a05a43f41777782d48c2b0fdb5e1a1c2 passed.
- The sase pin was not moved because sase calls no new binding; the scheduled ratchet picks the commit up.

evidence.note: Fix never landed: sase-1ou.land closed this bead (2026-10-28T20:58Z) after editing sase-core contention.rs (10 s budgets, release-after-start) and connection.rs (always open once and reopen after a quarantine), then ended its turn with sase plan propose. That handoff skips finalizers (agent_meta finalizer_status.phase stayed 'planned'; commit_results.json in artifacts ace-run/202610/27/20261027092233 lists only beads commits). sase-core origin/master has no commit after ed8328f9 (12:31 EDT) and the workspace sase_20 linked sase-core checkout is now clean, so the edits were discarded on workspace reuse. The flaky contention tests and the quarantine 'busy with no lock holder' product regression are therefore still present; the change must be redone. Root cause tracked as bob-cli-e0 (plan propose handoff never commits). Not reproduced the flake myself.
